question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[0,5],$ compute $P(X\le 3).$
question.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le x\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[0,5],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5},\, & 0\le x\le 5, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 3) & =P(0\le X\le 3) \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3-0}{5} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
